trails.name: River Bench Trail (#6045A), Browns Canyon NM
trails.distance: 5.5 mi round trip to the river

other_links.label: BLM — Browns Canyon National Monument
other_links.note: Managing authority. States 'Roundtrip to the river via the River Bench Trail (#6045A): 5.5 miles, 3 hours'; describes it as the gentle dead-end river-bench route.

other_links.label: Komoot — Turret Trail and River Bench Trail loop
other_links.note: The combined Turret + River Bench loop: 5.4 mi, 558 ft gain, moderate, 2 h 26 min.

other_links.label: Gaia GPS — Ruby Mountain via Turret 6045 and River Bench 6045A
other_links.note: Same combination recorded as a moderate out-and-back.

trails.stats_note: BLM's 5.5 mi is the round trip to the river and is the figure to plan on. AllTrails has no page for #6045A on its own; the 5.4 mi Komoot figure is the Turret+River Bench loop, not this trail alone.

trails.name: Turret Trail (#6045), Browns Canyon NM
trails.distance: 2.7 mi round trip to the river at Little Cottonwood

other_links.label: BLM — Browns Canyon National Monument
other_links.note: Authority: 'Roundtrip to river at Little Cottonwood via Turret Trail (#6045): 2.7 miles, 2 hours'; a steep but short hike with wide views.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Browns Canyon National Monument area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page; source of the 4.5 star / 555 review figure.

trails.stats_note: Distance is BLM's 2.7 mi round trip; the AllTrails rating is for its own 'Turret Trail' listing, which does not publish a matching length in the indexed snippet.

trails.name: Elkhart Park — Photographer's Point

alltrails.name: Photographers Point via Pole Creek Trail

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Photographers Point
other_links.note: Starts at Elkhart Park trailhead on the Pole Creek Trail, ~4.5 mi of sub-alpine forest climbing; about 4 hours round trip.

trails.stats_note: Our entry names the trailhead; AllTrails indexes the hike itself under the Pole Creek Trail. Takes about 4-4.5 hr.

trails.name: Green River Lakes / Highline Trail

alltrails.name: Green River Lakes to Summit Lake via Highline Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Green River Lakes Loop
other_links.note: The realistic day option instead of the full Highline: shores of Upper and Lower Green River Lakes, 4.8 stars from 460 reviews.

other_links.label: USFS — Hike the Highline Trail
other_links.note: Forest Service page for the Highline; notes the west-side lakeshore trail is less well marked than the official east-side trail.

trails.stats_note: 35.8 mi / 4,009 ft is a 14.5-16 hr backpack, not a day walk from camp — the Green River Lakes Loop link is the one worth planning around.

trails.name: Sinks Canyon (Popo Agie Falls)

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Popo Agie Falls
other_links.note: Trailhead is Bruce's Parking Area on Shoshone National Forest land, 3 miles up the road from the Sinks Canyon State Park visitor center.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Popo Agie Falls Trail
other_links.note: Confirms the falls-overlook route and its high viewpoint.

trails.stats_note: No distance or difficulty could be sourced from the indexed snippet, so none is recorded. Note the trail leaves from Shoshone NF, not from inside the state park.

trails.name: Oregon Trail Pathway

other_links.label: OutsideAtlas — Oregon Trail, Gering NE
other_links.note: Lists it as an easy hiking trail in Gering with map and access detail.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing is titled just 'Oregon Trail'; its own text confirms it by describing the covered wagons at the Scotts Bluff NM administrative building as the start of the Oregon Trail Pathway. No star rating or length could be sourced, so neither is recorded.

trails.name: Prairie View Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Prairie View Trail
other_links.note: Authority: the only trail in Scotts Bluff NM that allows bicycling; best views of Saddle Rock eastbound, Mitchell Pass westbound.

other_links.label: NPS — Bicycling at Scotts Bluff National Monument
other_links.note: Source of the 1.2-mile paved length, visitor center to the monument's eastern boundary.

trails.stats_note: Bike-legal status is the NPS's own statement, not inferred. It connects to Gering's Monument Valley Pathway.

trails.name: Lover's Leap Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lovers' Leap (short version)
other_links.note: A separate 2.5 mi out-and-back listing to the overlook only, +531 ft, 4.6 stars from 218 reviews — the shorter option on the same hill.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 2-2.5 hr. AllTrails spells it 'Lovers'' where our card spells it 'Lover's'.

trails.name: Castle Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in Badlands
other_links.note: Authority: 10.2 mi / 16.45 km round trip, moderate; longest established trail in the park, Door and Window lot to Fossil Exhibit Trail.

other_links.label: NPS — Castle Trailhead
other_links.note: Five miles one way, relatively level.

trails.stats_note: NPS says 10.2 mi round trip, AllTrails 10.3 mi — the same trail, measured twice. No shade the whole way. About 3.5-4 hr.

trails.name: Cliff Shelf Nature Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in Badlands
other_links.note: Authority: 0.86 mi / 1.38 km round trip, graded moderate; boardwalks, stairs and natural path through junipers.

other_links.label: NPS — Cliff Shelf Trailhead
other_links.note: One of the few shaded spots in the park — a juniper grove.

trails.stats_note: NPS calls it 0.86 mi and moderate; AllTrails 0.5 mi and easy. The stairs are the reason for the harder official grade. AllTrails records dogs as not allowed on this trail.

trails.name: Window Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Window Trailhead
other_links.note: Authority: short accessible boardwalk to a natural window in the Badlands Wall. NPS lists 0.26 mi / 0.41 km round trip, easy, ~20 minutes.

trails.stats_note: Accessible boardwalk the whole way — the one Badlands trail that needs no ability at all.

trails.name: Bloody Knife Trail

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.9 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Bloody Knives Loop
other_links.note: Mapped as part of the Fort Abraham Lincoln trail network.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Bloody Knife's Loop
other_links.note: Graded intermediate.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing; ND Parks & Recreation is the authority confirming it exists, with the length and the permitted uses.

trails.name: Little Soldier Loop

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.8 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'.

other_links.label: Komoot — Little Soldier Loop
other_links.note: Parking at the main park entrance or near the visitor center.

other_links.label: Gaia GPS — Little Soldier Loop
other_links.note: Independently records 1.8 miles, matching the park.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing. Two community sources and the park agree on 1.8 mi.

trails.name: Mato-tope Trail

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.4 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, mountain biking' — no horses on this one, unlike its neighbours.

other_links.label: ND Tourism — Mato-tope Trail
other_links.note: Begins at the confluence of the Missouri and Heart rivers, looping through the campground; named for the Mandan chief Four Bears.

trails.stats_note: Park and AllTrails agree at 1.4 mi. Takes about 0.5-1 hr.

trails.name: Scouts Trail System

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 8.8 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'. The backbone of the park's ~20 mile non-motorised network.

other_links.label: National Recreation Trails — Scout's Trail
other_links.note: Federally designated National Recreation Trail inside the park.

trails.stats_note: Named as a system rather than a single path, but the park publishes it as one 8.8 mi entity with one set of permitted uses, so it is kept as listed. No AllTrails page.

trails.name: Young Hawk Interpretive Trail

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.1 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'. Vistas over On-A-Slant Village, the Missouri and Heart rivers and Bismarck.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Young Hawk Interpretive Loop
other_links.note: Mapped within the park network.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing; ND Parks & Recreation confirms it with length and uses.

trails.name: Aiton Heights Fire Tower Trail

other_links.label: onX — Aiton Heights Fire Tower
other_links.note: Records a 2.2-mile in-and-out to the tower, which was moved to Itasca in 1937 for fire detection.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails indexes it as 'Itasca Fire Tower Trail'; the 2.2 mi figure is onX's, not AllTrails', and no AllTrails length could be sourced.

trails.name: Bohall Trail

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: Averages 17 minutes; good for birding. No star rating could be sourced, so none is recorded (the listing carries 52 reviews).

trails.name: Dr. Roberts Trail

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: The ~1.9 mi comes from a secondary write-up, not from AllTrails or the DNR, so treat it as approximate. Quiet forest walk along Lyendecker Lake and Lake Itasca.

trails.name: Mississippi Headwaters Trail

other_links.label: Explore Minnesota — Mississippi River headwaters at Itasca
other_links.note: Context for the headwaters and the wider Mississippi River Trail.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca State Park
other_links.note: Authority for the park; the walk across the Mississippi at its outlet.

trails.stats_note: Starts at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center and is mostly flat. No length or difficulty could be sourced from the indexed snippet.

not_a_trail.name: Preacher's Grove Trail
not_a_trail.what_it_really_is: A roadside old-growth red pine grove and overlook, not a named hiking trail. The MN DNR's own Itasca summer trails map lists it as a stop on the Main Park Drive tour — 'Include stops at Preacher's Grove and Peace Pipe Vista overlooks' — and it is also a stop on the park's paved multi-use bike trail. No trail database carries a listing of this name, and the DNR does not publish a length for it. Worth stopping at; there is no walk to record.

trails.name: Duluth Lakewalk

other_links.label: City of Duluth — Lakewalk
other_links.note: Authority: nearly eight miles of paved pedestrian and bicycle trail, Canal Park to Brighton Beach (Kitchi Gammi Park).

other_links.label: TrailLink — Duluth Lakewalk
other_links.note: Rail-trail style listing, Canal Park Museum to 26th Ave East & London Rd.

other_links.label: AllTrails — The Lakewalk: Brighton Beach Park
other_links.note: The far north-east section through Brighton Beach Park with rocky shoreline access.

trails.stats_note: Paved and bike-legal per the City of Duluth — the strongest cruising candidate at this stop. Averages 2 h 19 min end to end.

trails.name: Enger Park / Enger Tower Trail

other_links.label: City of Duluth — Enger Park
other_links.note: Authority for the park; Enger Tower was built in 1939, and the park also holds the American-Japanese Peace Bell.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Enger Park
other_links.note: A 3-mile out-and-back around the viewpoint over Duluth, St. Louis Bay and Lake Superior.

other_links.label: Komoot — Enger Tower
other_links.note: Collects the various short walks and longer routes that reach the tower.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Enger Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page. AllTrails' best-rated route here is 'Lift Bridge to Enger Tower via Superior Hiking Trail', 4.2 stars from 158 reviews — a much longer approach than walking up in the park.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails page for a trail of this name; only a park browse page and a long Superior Hiking Trail approach from the Lift Bridge. Distance and difficulty are therefore not recorded.

trails.name: Hawk Ridge Nature Reserve Trails

alltrails.name: Plantation, Amity Creek, Powerline, Ridge Loop and Hawk Ridge Trail

other_links.label: Hawk Ridge Bird Observatory — trail maps
other_links.note: The managing organisation's own trail maps for the reserve.

other_links.label: Hawk Ridge Bird Observatory — Hawk Ridge Trails
other_links.note: Trail descriptions and current conditions, including leaf-colour reporting.

other_links.label: City of Duluth — Hawk Ridge
other_links.note: 235 acres of undeveloped land on the highest point of eastern Skyline Parkway; established 1972.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Hawk Ridge Nature Reserve area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page; names Ole's Trail, Middle Trail and the Ridge Loop Trail as the connected path along the rocky ledges.

trails.stats_note: This is a network rather than one path, so the AllTrails link is the composite loop that strings its trails together, not an exact-name match. No single length or difficulty applies.

trails.name: Jay Cooke State Park — Swinging Bridge & river gorge trails

other_links.label: MN DNR — Jay Cooke summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Authority: names the Silver Creek Trail (Hiking Club Trail) as a 3.5-mile loop that crosses the Swinging Bridge and climbs from the river — mowed grass and bare rock, some hills.

other_links.label: The Outbound — Carlton Trail at Jay Cooke
other_links.note: The south-bank river route from the River Inn visitor centre.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Jay Cooke State Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page.

trails.stats_note: Our entry covers the bridge plus a cluster of gorge trails rather than one named route, so no single AllTrails page matches. The DNR's 3.5 mi Silver Creek loop is the concrete version of this walk.

trails.name: Artist's Point

other_links.label: North Shore Visitor — Artist's Point & Grand Marais Harbor
other_links.note: Local guide to the point and the cobblestone harbour walk.

trails.stats_note: Two ways out to the lighthouse — over the rocks, or along the concrete break wall, which is narrow and has no barriers or ropes. Worth knowing before taking a dog.

trails.name: Devil's Kettle, Judge C.R. Magney State Park

other_links.label: MN DNR — Judge C.R. Magney State Park
other_links.note: Authority: the popular hike leads upstream along the Brule River to Devil's Kettle, where the river splits around volcanic rock.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Judge C.R. Magney park map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park map.

other_links.label: North Shore Experiences — Judge C.R. Magney
other_links.note: Puts the hike at 2.5 miles round trip out of the park's 7 miles of trail.

trails.stats_note: The 2.5 mi round trip is a local guide's figure, not AllTrails' or the DNR's. There are a lot of stairs on the river climb.

trails.name: Shovel Point & Palisade Head, Tettegouche State Park

other_links.label: AllTrails — Palisade Head
other_links.note: The other half of our entry, listed separately: 4.5 stars from 483 reviews, panoramic Lake Superior cliff views.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Tettegouche State Park
other_links.note: Authority: sea caves, a sea stack and Palisade Head.

other_links.label: Lake Superior Circle Tour — Shovel Point Trail
other_links.note: Calls it a 1.9 mile out-and-back from behind the visitor centre and grades it easy.

trails.stats_note: Our card pairs two places AllTrails lists separately; the figures here are Shovel Point's. Distance differs by source (AllTrails 1.4 mi, Circle Tour 1.9 mi) and so does the grade — 64% of AllTrails reviewers call it moderate, the Circle Tour calls it easy. Palisade Head is a separate drive-up cliff.

trails.name: Superior Hiking Trail — Pincushion Mountain segment

alltrails.name: Pincushion Mountain via Superior Hiking Trail

other_links.label: USFS — Pincushion Mountain Trails
other_links.note: Superior National Forest authority page: the view down to Grand Marais, its harbour and lighthouse, with picnic tables at the trailhead.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Pincushion Mountain Overlook via Superior Hiking Trail
other_links.note: The short version — out to the summit overlook only, over boardwalks and rock, instead of the full 10.3 mi segment.

other_links.label: Superior Hiking — Pincushion Mountain Lookout Trail
other_links.note: Access is 3 miles up the Gunflint Trail from Grand Marais.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails grades the full segment challenging and averages 4 h 39 min. The overlook-only listing is the realistic afternoon option. No star rating could be sourced for either.

trails.name: Big Bay State Park trails, Madeline Island

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Big Bay State Park hiking
other_links.note: Authority: the Point trail connects with the Bay View Trail near the tip, 1.7 miles including a loop with inland and shoreline segments.

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Big Bay State Park
other_links.note: Sandstone bluffs along 4 miles of Lake Superior shoreline, plus a 1-mile boardwalk.

other_links.label: Komoot — hiking in Big Bay State Park
other_links.note: Routes across the sandstone bluffs, barrier beach and lagoon.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Big Bay State Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page.

trails.stats_note: Our entry is the park's trails collectively; the AllTrails link is its most-reviewed single trail. The DNR's 1.7 mi is for the Point trail, not the whole network. Reaching it needs the Madeline Island ferry.

trails.name: Houghton Falls State Natural Area

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Houghton Falls State Natural Area No. 638
other_links.note: Authority: protects unfragmented Lake Superior shoreline supporting bald eagle, merlin, veery, wood thrush and Canada warbler.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 0.5-1 hr. AllTrails publishes no difficulty grade for it, so none is recorded. The 76-acre natural area is just north of Washburn; sandstone cliffs run down into the lake with a beach at the end.

trails.name: Mainland Sea Caves near Meyers Beach

alltrails.name: Meyers Beach Sea Caves via Lakeshore Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in the Apostle Islands
other_links.note: Authority: from Meyers Beach the trail runs first to the Crevasse, then above the mainland sea caves, then through woods to the campsites.

other_links.label: Travel Wisconsin — Lakeshore Trail at Meyers Beach
other_links.note: Breaks the sections down: 1.8 miles to the Crevasse, 2.4 miles above the sea caves.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lakeshore Trail Campsite via Meyers Beach
other_links.note: The longer continuation out to the campsite.

trails.stats_note: This is a clifftop hiking trail ABOVE the caves — the caves themselves are reached by kayak in summer and only over the ice in a hard winter, which is not a walk. AllTrails records it as dog-friendly. Sectional distances are Travel Wisconsin's; no single AllTrails length was in the snippet.

trails.name: Escarpment Trail

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Porcupine Mts Escarpment Trail
other_links.note: State tourism authority: a high rocky bluff with alpine-like vistas over the park interior.

other_links.label: Michigan Trail Maps — Escarpment Trail
other_links.note: Detailed route description along the ridgeline.

trails.stats_note: The westernmost section follows the ridge north of Lake of the Clouds. No length or grade was in the indexed snippet, so none is recorded. (Ignore a low-quality third-party page describing an 'Escarpment Trail' 4x4 route — that is not this hiking trail.)

trails.name: Lake of the Clouds overlook walkway

alltrails.name: Lake of the Clouds Overlook Loop

other_links.label: The Porcupine Mountains & Ontonagon Area — Lake of the Clouds
other_links.note: Confirms the overlook is reached by a fully accessible walkway — the most photographed feature in the park.

other_links.label: MyHikes — Lake of the Clouds Overlook
other_links.note: Records a 0.2-mile out-and-back and warns of crowds in peak foliage season.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lake of the Clouds (backcountry route)
other_links.note: A separate, primitive foot-traffic-only route looking down on the lake from several angles — 824 reviews. Not the accessible walkway.

trails.stats_note: Short accessible loop with several viewing points, about half a mile of walking in total. No star rating could be sourced.

trails.name: Presque Isle River waterfall loop (East + West River Trails)

alltrails.name: West River Trail and East River Trail Loop

other_links.label: AllTrails — Presque Isle Falls Loop
other_links.note: The same waterfalls under a different listing, 530 reviews, described as good for kids and families.

other_links.label: Michigan Trail Maps — East-West River Trails
other_links.note: In its final mile the Presque Isle drops more than 100 feet through a steep-sided gorge; the East River Trail is the harder side.

other_links.label: MyHikes — Presque Isle River Waterfalls Loop
other_links.note: Moderate 3-mile hike taking in Manabezho, Manido and Nawadaha Falls.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 1-1.5 hr. Reviewers warn it is NOT a loop during spring thaw, when high water cuts the link between the east and west trails and park maps do not show it. No star rating could be sourced for this listing.

trails.name: Summit Peak observation tower

other_links.label: The Porcupine Mountains & Ontonagon Area — Summit Peak
other_links.note: Climb to the top of the old watch tower for panoramic views over the wilderness.

trails.stats_note: Out-and-back, about 0.5-1 hr. Highest point in the Porcupine Mountains at 1,958 ft, with a 50-foot tower on top. AllTrails publishes no difficulty grade, so none is recorded.

trails.name: Union Mine Interpretive Trail

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Porcupine Mts Union Mine Trail
other_links.note: State tourism authority: a waterfall trail rich with copper-mining history.

other_links.label: Michigan Trail Maps — Union Mine Trail
other_links.note: Best when water is high or during spring runoff.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 0.5-1 hr; AllTrails grades it moderately challenging. Ten interpretive plaques on the loop. Park entry needs a Michigan Recreation Passport for the vehicle; arriving on foot or by bicycle does not.

trails.name: Visitor Center Nature Trail

alltrails.name: Porcupine Mountain Wilderness Visitor Center Trail Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Porcupine Mountains Visitor Center
other_links.note: Authority for the visitor centre this trail loops from.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 0.5-1 hr; a flat interpretive loop. No star rating could be sourced.

trails.name: Hogback Mountain Trail

other_links.label: Travel Marquette — Hogback Mountain
other_links.note: City tourism authority page with trail and seasonal information.

other_links.label: onX — Hogback Mountain
other_links.note: Puts it at about 4 miles out-and-back; trailhead off Beagle Club Road.

trails.stats_note: About 5 miles north of downtown Marquette off County Road 550. Marked with white/blue blazes; mostly flat until a steep rock finish to a 360-degree view. AllTrails says 3.2 mi, onX about 4 mi.

trails.name: Presque Isle Park loop trails (Black Rocks)

other_links.label: AllTrails — Presque Isle Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page for the forested peninsula at the north tip of Marquette.

trails.stats_note: No length or difficulty could be sourced from AllTrails for this listing, so neither is recorded — a secondary site puts the loop at about 2.2 mi and easy, which is worth confirming on the ground. Black Rocks is the cliff section on the loop — 20-to-30-foot volcanic cliffs locals jump from; it is a feature of this park, not a separate trail.

trails.name: Sugarloaf Mountain Trail

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Sugarloaf Mountain
other_links.note: State tourism authority: a short hike to arguably the best view in the Upper Peninsula.

trails.stats_note: Summit is 470 feet above the lake, reached by a 3,200-foot trail with dedicated pathways and wooden stairways — short, steep and stepped rather than long.

trails.name: Munising Falls Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Munising Falls
other_links.note: Authority: a paved 800-foot trail up a cool shaded canyon along Munising Creek to a 50-foot waterfall, inside the city limits where Washington Street becomes Sand Point Road.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Munising Falls (point of interest)
other_links.note: AllTrails carries the falls only as a point of interest, not as its own trail listing.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails trail page exists for this walk — only a point-of-interest entry and a 42.4-mile Lakeshore Trail backpacking route that passes it. The NPS confirms the trail and its length. Paved and very short.

trails.name: Clark Lake Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Authority: 'Clark Lake Loop (5.2 miles)', with a warning that conditions vary, fallen trees and wet areas are likely and cell service is minimal.

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Tahquamenon Falls Clark Lake Loop
other_links.note: Open to hiking, cross-country skiing and snowshoeing; begins at the Clark Lake Road parking lot and runs through pine forest.

trails.stats_note: Permitted uses are Michigan.org's — hiking, XC ski and snowshoe, with no mention of bikes. A recent AllTrails review measured the loop at 5.3 mi. Neither AllTrails nor the DNR publishes a difficulty grade for it, and no star rating could be sourced, so neither is recorded.

trails.name: Giant Pines Loop

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Tahquamenon Falls Giant Pines Trail
other_links.note: Authority: a 3.8-mile hiking trail through hemlocks and streams, named for two giant white pines on the route.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Giant Pines Loop Trail
other_links.note: Graded intermediate.

trails.stats_note: Michigan.org says 3.8 mi, AllTrails 3.5 mi. Takes about 1-1.5 hr and AllTrails reviewers describe it as good for children and families.

trails.name: Lower Falls island loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map covering the Lower Falls area.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing describes about 0.2 miles paved plus 0.4 miles of gravel road along the river with falls views, and notes loaner wheelchairs at the 'Fact Shack' by the Upper Falls parking lot. The river splits around a wooded midstream island reached by an island bridge or by rented rowboat. No star rating could be sourced; the listing carries 1,600 reviews.

trails.name: Tahquamenon River Trail (Lower Falls to Upper Falls)

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map for the river trail between the two falls.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 3.5-4 hr. The ground around the Lower Falls gets very muddy; accessible toilets at both ends and an off-road track chair is available. AllTrails' park page gives this trail 4.6 stars but the review count was not legible in the snippet, so no rating is recorded.

trails.name: Tahquamenon Falls Wilderness Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: Graded moderately challenging, averaging about 3 hours. Quiet — the listing carries only 46 reviews and no star rating could be sourced.
